meaning.zh:
“摊得太薄” 或 “分散精力太多”。

这个短语来源于涂抹黄油或果酱时，如果你将其涂抹得太薄，那么整体的口感和体验就会受到影响。借此比喻，如果一个人在太多事情上分散了精力或资源，那么他在每一件事情上的表现可能都会受到影响，无法做好。
meaning.en: This phrase originates from the idea of spreading butter or jam too thinly on a piece of bread, where the overall taste and experience are diminished. By extension, it implies that if someone is involved in too many tasks, their focus and resources are spread too thin to perform well in any single task.

lines.en: He's *spread too thin* with all his commitments and can't dedicate enough time to any one project.
lines.zh: 他有太多的承诺，精力分散，无法专注于任何一个项目。

lines.en: If you *spread yourself too thin*, you won't be able to give your best effort to any of your tasks.
lines.zh: 如果你让自己摊得太薄，就无法在任何任务上尽全力。

lines.en: She realized she had *spread herself too thin* by trying to balance work, school, and social life.
lines.zh: 她意识到自己试图平衡工作、学业和社交生活，从而让自己摊得太薄了。
